mappings.note: The laws of reflection applied to sound. Curriculum 82 has no outcome for reflection of sound at all; CG2's 'understands scientific principles and laws based on observations and analysis' is the only honest anchor. Recorded as a frame gap rather than forced onto LO-75, which is about naming buildings.
Two SONAR depths computed and subtracted. LO-79 is earned twice over; CG2 carries the SONAR content that no outcome names. The subtraction is what separates it from the single-target depth items.
The 17.2 m minimum-echo distance from d = vt/2. Same pairing as the other echo numericals, because the frame gives echo no outcome and the only discriminator left is the computation.
Two setups differing only in whether a medium is present - LO-4 and nothing more. Not LO-3: neither setup is a solid or a liquid, so no cross-medium comparison is made.

The 0.1 s persistence-of-hearing threshold. It belongs neither to a wave characteristic nor to any listed outcome; a single goal-level code rather than stretching LO-73, which is about loudness and pitch in music.

Reverberation control in an auditorium. LO-75 ('buildings designed for echoes') is the one code in the set about architecture shaped by sound reflection, so it fits an acoustic-design item better than any characteristics outcome; CG2 for the reflection physics itself.
Asks only for the NAME of the phenomenon (reverberation). No building is designed or remedied, so LO-75 is not earned here - that is what separates it from O53.
Ultrasonic defined by a frequency threshold, so LO-6 supplies frequency; CG2 carries the ultrasonic category, which no outcome names.
Bat echolocation as a real-life phenomenon whose MECHANISM must be reconstructed - LO-77's 'analyse real-life events and identify the key factors'. CG2 for ultrasound, which has no outcome.

A list of four ultrasound technologies to be recognised, with no mechanism to analyse and nothing to compute. CG2 alone; recorded as a poor fit, since applications of ultrasound appear nowhere in the frame.
A one-step SONAR depth. Shares CG2 + LO-79 with the other sonar numericals; they honestly differ only in the numbers.
Infrasound identified by frequency band (LO-6), applied to elephants. CG2 for the infrasonic category. Not LO-77: the item is recall of which animal, not an analysis of how communication works.
Defines vibration as the cause of sound - LO-2's exact claim. Not LO-1, which needs several production methods; this is the bare definition.
Names the vibrating PART in a particular source (vocal cords), which is LO-1's 'production ... through vibration of ...'. Not LO-2, which is the general causal statement rather than a named part.
Asks which laboratory INSTRUMENT is used for sound experiments, so C8.2's 'accurately uses scientific instruments' leads, with LO-1 for the tuning fork as a sound source.
Defines 'medium'. LO-4 is the outcome that introduces the term; LO-3 would be for comparing media, and none are compared here.
Asks what the bell jar experiment SIGNIFIES, so the conclusion (LO-4) plus C8.2 for drawing an inference from an experiment.
One reason, and it is LO-4's claim verbatim. No second code: the item is too small to probe anything else.
Compression versus rarefaction by density and pressure - LO-5. Shares the outcome with the other compression/rarefaction items because the frame has one longitudinal-wave row.
Asks for the term 'mechanical wave', defined by the need for a medium - LO-4.
Longitudinal versus transverse particle vibration, LO-5's statement. Same as O16 and honestly so.
The salt-grain demonstration shows sound carrying energy, which has no outcome in this frame (CG2), and asks what would be OBSERVED, which is C8.2's inference from an activity.
The microphone converts acoustic energy into an electrical signal. Nothing in the legal set covers transduction or sound technology; CG2 alone, recorded as a poor fit.
A crest on a density graph IS a compression, so this is the longitudinal structure again (LO-5) rather than LO-6's measurement of a characteristic.
The dashed line is the undisturbed mean density about which particles oscillate - LO-5. Pairs with V71 as two halves of the same graph and shares its outcome.
